note:
Lenton Avenue read off the enumerators' pages for 1881 and 1891, transcribed by A. Hagues and checked line by line before import.

**The record held nothing whatever for 1881 on this street.** All seventeen 1881 households here are new - a hundred and six people, from William S Birkin at Glenelg on the corner to Frederick Wadsworth at Newlands, which is now 33.

**The 1881 enumerator numbered almost nothing.** Eleven of the seventeen households on his 1881 round carry no house number at all, only the street. Those are left unfiled rather than guessed at from their position in his walk; the six he did number are filed. The 1891 enumerator numbered everything, so that year files almost completely.

**One household in the record is one person short.** Reuben Thompson's at 10 Lenton Avenue holds five of its six - the coachman, his wife, and three working sons - and wants only young Fred Upton, a scholar, who is created here.

**Four 1891 households are already complete in the record** - 14, 12, 6 and 4 Lenton Avenue - and are included only so that the columns the record has never carried for them, the marital status and the schedule number, can be filled in. Nothing about those people is changed.

Dundee House is 17 Lenton Avenue and Fernleigh is 11; both are filed by number under the names the record already keeps for them.
source: 1881 and 1891 census enumerators' pages for Lenton Avenue, Nottingham, transcribed by A. Hagues.
